_Story by Tom Perkins_

Mike Rogers, the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan, earned over
$420,000 during his tenure as a board member for a consultancy that is now
helping Pete Hegseth plan the next phase of the disastrous Iran war, according
to tax filings.

The MITRE Corporation is coordinating the controversial [Project Meridian:
"The Future of
Warfare,"](https://media.defense.gov/2026/Sep/30/2004009287/-1/-1/1/COMMISSIONING-
OF-PROJECT-MERIDIAN.PDF) which is bringing together weapons manufacturers and
tech leaders like Elon Musk to map out the future of U.S. warfare in Iran and
beyond. Some have [raised
questions](https://theintercept.com/2026/10/08/hegseth-military-ai-drones-
autonomous-war/) over [conflicts of
interest](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/06/nx-s1-5991899/elon-musk-palmer-
luckey-pentagon-drones-ai) among those leading the project.

Rogers, an establishment war hawk and former member of Congress, served on
MITRE's board of trustees, including a stint as its chair, for six years
through 2023. He left as he launched his first campaign for U.S. Senate during
the 2024 election. The company's CEO said Rogers was brought on for his "vast
national security expertise," and [IRS records
detail](https://projects.propublica.org/nonprofits/organizations/42239742/202443199349317359/full)
his annual earnings.

Rogers' support for the operation in Iran has been a liability throughout the
race against his opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.

"People say, well, 'What date is it going to end?' It shouldn't be a date. It
should be conditional," Rogers [told a right wing podcast
host](http://youtube.com/watch?v=DelHa-qFoWo) in March. "This is why Americans
need to stop for a minute, come together and say, 'let's get this done, get it
done right.'"

The war is among the drivers of stubborn, ongoing inflation and high gas
prices, and [polls
show](https://www.clickondetroit.com/news/local/2026/09/09/do-michigan-voters-
approve-trumps-handling-of-war-with-iran-here-are-the-latest-poll-
results/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) as many as 67% of Michigan voters disapprove
of it. El-Sayed has hammered Rogers over his support for endless wars, and
Rogers in recent weeks [waffled](https://www.metrotimes.com/news/mike-rogers-
has-a-new-position-on-the-iran-war-again/) on the operation in Iran, telling
Fox News that "we need to start wrapping it down."

The El-Sayed and Rogers campaigns did not respond to requests for comment.

Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Sept. 30[
announced](https://media.defense.gov/2026/Sep/30/2004009287/-1/-1/1/COMMISSIONING-
OF-PROJECT-MERIDIAN.PDF) the MITRE-led Project Meridian as "an effort led by
America's best minds to study the future of warfare." Hegseth named Musk,
former Republican Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich, and Palmer Luckey,
founder of defense technology company Anduril Industries, as top officials.

Former defense officials [noted to
NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/06/nx-s1-5991899/elon-musk-palmer-luckey-
pentagon-drones-ai) that the project's leaders could guide the U.S. to build
more space assets or rely more on drones that Musk's and Luckey's companies
produce, while making fewer tanks or other military equipment that they do not
make. Musk is [among Rogers' largest
supporters](https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/politics/2026/09/09/michigan-
senate-race-elon-musk-mike-rogers-abdul-el-sayed/91672511007/), backing him
via the America PAC that Musk finances.

"There are a lot of issues impacting this race, but everyone understands that
the Iran war is a primary reason for the high cost of gasoline and diesel,"
said Bernie Porn, a Michigan pollster who found El-Sayed [with a small lead
over Rogers](https://ssl2002.webhosting.comcast.net/epic-
mra/press/Stwd_Survey_Aug2026_Media_Freq.pdf) in late August. "And that is why
you see states like Iowa and Kansas in play, so this is one more thing to tie
Rogers to support for the Iran war."

_Tom Perkins is a freelance reporter in Detroit who covers the antiwar
movement locally and nationally._
